verdict.question: Two live denominators for one ratchet: gate/admission.sh pinned 473 (all-position tokens minus whole-file exemptions) while this ledger measured 335 code-position sites in canonical files. Which is the enforced budget?
verdict.ruling: CODE-POSITION. A `std.` inside a `#` comment or a `"` text literal resolves no home, reaches no world, and cannot violate law.std.zero -- it is prose, or it is a detector's own needle. The all-position count is not a measurement of the rule the ratchet enforces.

arithmetic.old_budget: 473 = 512 (tail-required tokens, all positions) - 39 (whole-file pins over 6 gate scanners)

decomposition.123: text/comment tokens charged outside the 6 pinned files: (88 text + 74 comment with tail) - 39 pinned
decomposition.15: code-position reaches in files that are not canonical debt: 14 historical + 1 the law.std.zero compile-fail fixture

does_this_raise_the_budget.answer: NO. It lowers the enforced number and REMOVES headroom rather than creating it.
does_this_raise_the_budget.why: 473 was not slack the tree was consuming -- the tree measured exactly 473 -- but 123 of those 473 were comment and string mentions. Deleting 123 characters of prose would have bought 123 new real reaches with no gate objection. Under code-position accounting a comment is worth nothing, so nothing can be sold to buy a reach.
does_this_raise_the_budget.headroom_before: 123 real code reaches purchasable by deleting prose
does_this_raise_the_budget.exemptions_before: 6 files, WHOLE-FILE: any future std. in them, code or not, rode in free under a pinned integer
does_this_raise_the_budget.exemptions_after: 3 files, 15 code-position reaches, each pinned exactly and each with a stated non-migratable reason
does_this_raise_the_budget.rule_b_before: the 6 pinned files were exempt from the added-line rule entirely, so a real reach added to gate/idiom.id passed unseen

hand_merge_when_shadow_clean_lands.conflict: reconcile/shadow-clean-20260822 moves the budget 473 -> 350; this lane moves it 473 -> 317 and changes what is counted.
hand_merge_when_shadow_clean_lands.resolution: TAKE THIS LANE'S COUNTER, NOT ITS NUMBER. 350 is the all-class code-position total; 317 is that total minus the 15 pinned non-canonical reaches minus the 18 migrated here. Both branches agree the denominator is code position; they disagree on whether the historical and negative-fixture reaches are budget or exemption.
steps: 0. Note that main no longer carries a census at all. A merge that 'keeps main's admission.sh' keeps a gate with no budget.
1. Keep gate/admission.sh's SCANNER and census_all from this lane -- shadow-clean recounts, this lane changes HOW, and a recount over the old byte counter reintroduces the 123.

2. Keep gate/std-fixtures.manifest from this lane (3 code-position pins). shadow-clean's 350 has no exemption set, so the compile-fail fixture examples/compile_fail/world_std_os.id becomes budget the tree can never retire -- it MUST carry std.os.exit(1) or it stops being a fixture.

3. Set STD_BUDGET to whatever `sh gate/admission.sh --census-only` prints on the merged tree. Do not hand-pick it and do not carry 350 or 317 across the merge: both were measured on trees that no longer exist.
4. Re-run gate/admission-controls.sh. Its synthetic trees are built at the shipped budget, so a stale number turns the at-budget control red -- that is the intended alarm, not a control to relax.
5. If the merged number exceeds 317 + (code reaches on lines shadow-clean genuinely added), the merge reintroduced debt. Investigate rather than re-pinning upward.
hand_merge_when_shadow_clean_lands.already_done_for_main: This lane IS the hand-merge against c77dea60. gate/admission.sh here is main's file plus a census section; the quarantine half is unchanged from ee8adabf.

rebase_note_c77dea60.what_main_actually_does_now: The premise that main's gate/admission.sh 'reports 473 counted against budget 473' is STALE. Commit ee8adabf ('admission: remove false semantic registries', on main at c77dea60) DELETED the census outright, along with gate/std-fixtures.manifest and gate/vocabulary.admitted. main's admission.sh is an added-line quarantine only: it has no budget, no denominator, and no downward pressure on the reaches already in the tree.
rebase_note_c77dea60.mains_objection_was_right: Its header states it exactly: the census was 'a position-blind 473-token census and therefore created a second, false authority one commit after the ledger was published.' That is the same finding this lane reaches independently. The disagreement is only about the remedy.
rebase_note_c77dea60.why_deletion_is_the_wrong_remedy: A quarantine cannot ratchet. It stops the debt growing on added lines and does nothing about the 344 reaches already there, and it cannot notice a rewrite that relocates them. Between ee8adabf and this commit the only thing making the number fall was voluntary.
rebase_note_c77dea60.resolution_taken_here: Both rules, and they deliberately disagree about position. QUARANTINE (main's, kept byte-for-byte): raw `std.` on any added line, ANY position, no exemptions -- on an added line the cheap rule is the strong one. CENSUS (restored, position-accurate): charges only code-position reaches, because a budget that counts prose is a budget payable in prose.

migration_20260823.rule: Migrate only where the compiler itself names the canonical relation. No compatibility alias, no resolver shim, no namespace fallback, and no rename of one root to another.

files.semantic_diff: subject: the process exit status. relation: `exit`, a member edge of the `os` world (src/subject_home.zig os_dot_members, how=direct, face=relation, result=void -- measured to lower end to end). world: `os`, default-injected, so the anchor is not spelled. The `std` root is DELETED, not renamed: it owned no meaning and supplied no authority.
files.check_before: fail (law.std.zero refusal, the only one of 350 code sites the compiler catches)
files.second_blocker: DNB011 application 37 relation `chomp` unresolved-application-facts -- std.script.chomp, frozen debt

files.semantic_diff: The `io` world SUPPLIES a stream; it is not the stream. `read`/`close` are relations on the stream instance (src/subject_home.zig stream_relations), so the stream `f` becomes the subject and the world disappears from the source entirely -- it is a grant, not a receiver. `open` orients on the path per C0 law.world.grant canon `file = path:open()`.
files.second_blocker: SEMANTIC-VOCABULARY-BLOCKED: `open` is in NO relation space. src/subject_home.zig leaves it out of stream_relations deliberately -- 'its canon is path:open(), and path:open has no lowering anywhere in this tree, so listing it here would refuse the only spelling that works. Recorded as owed, not enforced.' The canon C0 names is unimplemented.
files.check_regression_is_exposure: The file's `check` passed only because `std.io.open` was an unresolved namespace projection nothing typed. `direct` already failed before the migration. Nothing in build.zig or gate/ consumes this file.

files.second_blocker: Same: `path:open` unadmitted. Its other 14 reaches stay: 13 `std.ml.export.onnx_*` (SEMANTIC-VOCABULARY-BLOCKED, no admitted ONNX relation, and the names are mashed compounds LAW-16 forbids) and 1 `std.encoding.json.decode` (SEMANTIC-VOCABULARY-BLOCKED, measured: `json:decode(x)` answers 'decode is neither a descriptor nor a callable').

deliberately_not_migrated.reason: Frozen debt. `script` is a namespace root that owns no meaning, and the relations behind it need structured command + process world vocabulary that does not exist. Measured: the fs subset has an explicit canonical mapping in AGENTS.md (`fs_exists` -> `path:exists()`, `fs_write` -> `path:write()`) and NEITHER relation resolves -- 'exists is neither a descriptor nor a callable'. SEMANTIC-VOCABULARY-BLOCKED.
deliberately_not_migrated.one_exception_is_ready: std.script.getenv(k, fallback) and std.script.getenv_or(k), 28 sites: the compiler names `env(k)` as the repair by hand and `env("HOME")` checks clean. NOT taken here because getenv falls back on BOTH nil and empty string while `env(k)` answers "" for a name set to empty -- a silent behaviour change in benchmark harnesses. Needs a per-site read, not a sweep.

deliberately_not_migrated.reason: SEMANTIC-VOCABULARY-BLOCKED. lib/time.id defines `monotonic` as `now_ns()` whose only body is `@comp.c.emit(...)` -- a retired directive namespace. The `os` roster's `clock` is a DIFFERENT fact (CPU time, not a monotonic wall clock) and is marked `.unrealized` anyway. Rewriting monotonic timing onto `clock()` would silently change what five benchmark harnesses measure.

deliberately_not_migrated.spelling: std.base64.* / std.crypto.rand.bytes / std.hash.* / std.bit.* / std.net.* / std.maps.* / std.table.* / std.reflect.* / std.strconv.* / std.fmt.*
deliberately_not_migrated.reason: SEMANTIC-VOCABULARY-BLOCKED. Each is a namespace-first dispatch whose subject-first form has no admitted relation. Inventing one would be the namespace this gap forbids, spelled differently.

world_grant_violations.class: CORRECTNESS FINDING, not migration debt. These are not files that merely spell `std.`; they are files whose call SHAPE violates C0 law.world.grant, and the `std.` prefix was HIDING that from the type checker.
world_grant_violations.law: C0 law.world.grant / law.subject.resolve, quoted in src/subject_home.zig: canon = 'file = path:open()'; deny = 'io:open(path)'; 'io:open(path) cannot become canonical merely because io is reachable'; fails = 'world authority arriving through ... namespace receiver'.
world_grant_violations.mechanism: `std.io.read(f, n)` passes the STREAM as the first operand of a relation reached through the `io` WORLD. The io world supplies stream instances; it is not itself a stream and has no `read`. Because the whole chain hung off the unresolved `std` root, sema's checkStreamRelationFace never saw it and `idol check` reported the files clean. Drop four characters and the refusal fires immediately.

sites.diagnostic_once_the_prefix_is_gone: 'read' is a relation on a stream, and 'f' is that stream: passing it as the first operand of 'io.read' makes the world stand in for the subject it only supplies -- write 'f:read(...)'

world_grant_violations.why_it_matters_beyond_these_two: The general lesson is the measurement, not the two files: a `std.` prefix SUPPRESSES semantic checking of everything downstream of it. 36 of the 40 canonical files pass `idol check` today; 4 of them stop passing the moment the prefix is removed. `check`-pass over a tree carrying 332 code-position reaches is not evidence of anything.

law_vs_implementation_conflict.finding: docs/spec/host.md and docs/spec/world.md both carry a 'RETRACTED under world reconciliation v2' paragraph ruling that `io` IS an ordinary world value and a legitimate subject, so `io:read()` and `io:write(x)` are CANONICAL. AGENTS.md restates it: 'I/O uses io:read / io:write, not io.read / io.write'. GAP-157's own ruling text names `io:read` as a canonical reach.
law_vs_implementation_conflict.measured: The compiler refuses both. `io:read()` answers "'read' is a relation on a stream, and the 'io' world is not a stream -- it SUPPLIES the stream ... write 'stdin:read(...)'" (src/sema.zig checkStreamRelationFace, citing law.world.grant). `io:write("x")` answers the same.
law_vs_implementation_conflict.so: sema enforces the RETRACTED v1 reading. One of the two must move, and this lane does not own either. Reported, not repaired.
law_vs_implementation_conflict.consequence_for_this_gap: The canonical target GAP-157 names for the 17 `std.io.*` sites does not compile. The only spelling that does is subject-first on the stream instance -- which is what this lane wrote, and which the v2 text also permits ('Where a stream is the real subject, it stays the subject').
law_vs_implementation_conflict.owner: GAP-154 (host boundary) with GAP-157; needs a ruling before any further io migration.

what_would_make_it_vacuous_and_does_not: A budget above the measured value: the gate prints 'census is N, UNDER the pinned budget' and demands the pin be lowered in the same commit.
An exemption for a file that stopped needing one: refused as EARNED OUT.
A pin of zero: refused by the manifest parser.
A missing or empty manifest: refused, rather than falling back to exempting nothing.
Zero or too few readable subjects: refused (GAP-201/GAP-220, via gate/subject.sh plus a MIN_SUBJECTS floor on files actually opened).
